_repo: Folder of the git checkout the checks read (branch and history). Example: C:\work\my-project
_expected_branch: Branch the package must be on. Example: main
_lock_file: Lock file the checker must not find held by a live process (no lock = fine). Example: C:\work\my-project\locks\checker.lock
_python: Absolute path of the Python that runs the checks (Python 3.12 recommended). Example: C:\Python312\python.exe
_min_free_bytes: Minimum free disk space in bytes before a check is allowed. Example: 2000000000 (2 GB)
_runner_log: Optional. Log file of the job runner; used to tell a stopped job from a running one.
_task_id: Optional. Id of the task whose log lines are checked. Example: task-042
_job_lock: Optional. Lock file of that job; a live pid in it means RUNNING, not abandoned.
_allowed_paths: Optional. Path prefixes or globs a patch may change. Empty list = no changes allowed; omit the key to skip the check.
_command_checks: Optional. Commands that must exit 0 and print the expected text. Example: a test run or a linter.
_result_rules: Optional. Labels that the brief must hold one result row for, per changed file (| label | file | result |). Empty list = off. Example: ["T1", "T2"]
_banned_commands: Optional. Text that must not appear in the brief.
_needs_human: Items a machine cannot judge. Always printed in the report under 'unverified'.
needs_human: decisions about money or access stay with the owner
